title: Ames: proper object of justifying fiducia is Christ — not the proposition ‘my sins are remitted’
source_text: XLIX. Ac cum fiducia illa qua Christo innitimur & ei adhaeremus, sit juxta Amesium, proprius & formalis fidei actus, qua justificans est, non debuit idem vir doctus mirari quod Amesius, eodem in loco dicat, proprium objectum fidei justificantis, qua talis, esse illud in quo fides acquiescit ad justificationem consequendam, nempe Christum, vel Dei misericordiam in Christo; non propositionem, vel axioma: & eo nomine Amesium exagitare, tanquam hominem absurdum, & nescientem quid dicat. Clarus est enim Amesii sensus: videlicet, ejus fiduciae qua Christo innitimur, & cui Amesius tribuit justificationem, tanquam actui proprio fidei, qua justificans est, immediatum & proprium objectum esse Christum ipsum, non vero hanc propositionem, mihi sunt per Christum remissa peccata: licet fides justificans, peracta justificatione, per alium actum attingat veritatem & certitudinem ejusdem propositionis. Quae ratio est, ut notat ibidem Amesius, cur nonnulli Theologi sic loquuntur, quasi ista propositio, mihi sunt per Christum remissa peccata, esset proprium objectum fidei justificantis.
pass_a_gloss: And since that trust by which we lean on Christ and adhere to Him is, according to Ames, the proper and formal act of faith as justifying, that same learned man ought not to have wondered that Ames says in the same place that the proper object of justifying faith as such is that in which faith rests unto obtaining justification — namely Christ, or God's mercy in Christ; not a proposition, or axiom: and on that account to harry Ames as an absurd man who does not know what he is saying. For Ames's sense is clear: namely, that of that trust by which we lean on Christ, and to which Ames attributes justification as the proper act of faith as justifying, the immediate and proper object is Christ Himself, not this proposition, my sins have been remitted to me through Christ: although justifying faith, after justification is accomplished, by another act attains the truth and certainty of the same proposition. Which is the reason, as Ames notes in the same place, why some Theologians so speak as if that proposition, my sins have been remitted to me through Christ, were the proper object of justifying faith.
pass_b_english: Ames: the fiducia that leans on Christ is faith’s proper formal justifying act.
Its proper object = Christ / God’s mercy in Christ — not a proposition or axiom.
Not ‘my sins are remitted through Christ’ as the immediate object.
After justification, another act may reach that proposition’s certainty.
Explains why some speak as if that remitted-proposition were faith’s proper object.
